What this crew builds and repairs

On the Suncoast the work starts with pavers: paver driveways, paver patios and walkways and pool deck pavers, with travertine and other stone for decks. The same crew handles paver cleaning and sealing and paver restoration, meaning stripping a worn sealer, lifting and relaying settled areas, replacing broken units and re-sanding the joints.

After pavers come concrete driveways, concrete pool decks, walkways, stamped concrete and concrete repair, plus artificial turf and retaining walls. Homeowners in Sarasota proper usually ask about sealing pavers in Sarasota and restoring pavers in Sarasota; east in the master-planned communities the same requests show up as paver restoration in Lakewood Ranch.

Sealing near salt water, and when pavers need restoring instead

Gulf air and pool chemistry are hard on a paver surface, and a coastal patio tends to show it sooner than an inland one. A sealer slows staining and keeps joint sand in place; it won't level a field that has dropped. When the surface is flat and only dull, wash, re-sand and seal. When it dips, rocks or pools water, the base needs attention first, and restoration is the job.

The paver industry's own guide gives no fixed interval for re-coating; it says sealers need renewing after a period of wear and weather (ICPI Tech Spec 5). Near the water we inspect more often and judge by what the surface is doing. This post on salt air and saltwater pools covers the coastal upkeep in more detail.

What changes when you build around Sarasota and Manatee

Nearly every lot in both counties is flatwoods sand with groundwater close to the surface. EauGallie and Immokalee, the two most common series, hold a seasonal high water table within about 6 to 18 inches (NRCS, EauGallie series; NRCS, Immokalee series), and Felda holds water within a foot for part of the year (NRCS, Felda series). For pavers that points to the thicker end of ICPI's range: 6 inches of compacted aggregate as the starting point, with 2 to 4 inches added where the soil stays wet (ICPI Tech Spec 2).

The coast adds layers. FEMA's Zone AE marks at least a 1-percent annual flood chance, and Zone VE adds wave action strong enough to damage structures (FEMA, Coastal FIRM features). Building seaward of the state's Coastal Construction Control Line needs a DEP permit on top of local approvals, and Sarasota County keeps its own Gulf Beach Setback Line (FDEP CCCL Program; Sarasota County Code §54-723). Siesta Key, Longboat Key and Anna Maria Island are where those lines come up most.

Rain is similar on both sides of the state. The Sarasota–Bradenton airport normal is 49.05 inches a year (NOAA 1991–2020 normals), concentrated between late May and mid-October. Watering rules are tighter than usual right now: the Southwest Florida Water Management District has both counties under a once-a-week order through March 31, 2027 (SWFWMD District Water Restrictions), one reason turf versus sod is a live question.

Permits: Sarasota County, Manatee County and the cities

As on the other coast, the driveway apron needs a right-of-way permit almost everywhere. Patios and pavers on private ground range from exempt to a zoning review, depending on which office has the address.

HOAs and architectural approvals in Lakewood Ranch and beyond

Lakewood Ranch generates the most paperwork questions. In the Country Club and Edgewater villages, a Modification Request Form has to be approved before a homeowner reseals, repaints or changes the material of a driveway or walkway, and the manual lists approved sealer colors (Lakewood Ranch Town Hall, CEVA Homeowners’ Manual). In North Venice, the Venetian Golf & River Club's committee takes applications until noon on the last Monday of the month (Venetian Golf & River Club POA, ACC Application), and Palmer Ranch leaves architectural review to its individual neighborhoods (Palmer Ranch Master Association). State law bars an HOA from requiring a building permit before it reviews your request (F.S. 720.3035). This Lakewood Ranch ARC guide walks through the steps.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Sarasota crew based?

In Sarasota, Florida. It's a service-area business with no storefront or street address, so the crew comes to you. The unit's Google Business Profile is set in Sarasota, and the crew covers Sarasota and Manatee counties.

Do you work in Lakewood Ranch, Venice, North Port and the islands?

Yes. Lakewood Ranch straddles the Sarasota–Manatee line, Venice and North Port are in Sarasota County, and Siesta Key, Longboat Key and Anna Maria Island are covered too. For a town that isn't listed, call (941) 207-7585 and ask.

Does sealing matter more near the Gulf?

Salt air, pool chemicals and a high water table are tough on a paver surface, so coastal owners often check theirs more often. There's no fixed re-seal date in the industry guide, so we judge by the surface: water no longer beading, joint sand gone, color fading unevenly.

Do I need approval before changing a Lakewood Ranch driveway?

In the Country Club and Edgewater villages, yes. A Modification Request Form comes first for sealing, repainting or overlaying a driveway or walkway. We can supply dimensions and materials for it; the association decides.

Do pavers near the beach need a state permit?

Seaward of the Coastal Construction Control Line, a DEP permit applies in addition to local approvals, and Sarasota County has its own Gulf Beach Setback Line on county beaches. We'll tell you at the visit if your lot falls near either line.

Does the Sarasota crew also work in Orlando?

No. Central Florida jobs go to the Kissimmee & Greater Orlando crew, which is based in Kissimmee and has a separate phone line.
